newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippines' Ramos slams justice system.
newsitem.headline: Philippines' Ramos slams justice system.

text.p: Filipinos will always feel they can get away with murder as long as the rich and powerful were able to flout the law, President Fidel Ramos said.

Ramos, castigating judges and lawyers in a speech on Saturday, said inept members of the bar and bench, incompetent prosecutors and perceptions that "the law is a plaything" of the elite was encouraging banditry.

Ramos's outburst was prompted by media reports linking some politicians to sex crimes against minors, the killing by a police colonel of a motorist in a quarrel during a traffic jam, and charges by a citizens group that his government was inept in dealing with crime.
Ramos announced on Saturday that he had appointed former justice secretary Silvestre Bello as solicitor general, replacing Raul Goco.
As chief state lawyer, Bello would be in charge of pursuing dozens of corruption cases pending against the family and business associates of late president Ferdinand Marcos.
The government has accused them of looting up to $10 billion from the economy during Marcos's 20-year rule, which ended with his ousting in a popular revolt in 1986.
